You are jolly_ember22, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, pale_kettle84, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.

# Ouch! `ouch` stands for **Obvious Unified Compression Helper**. It's a CLI tool for compressing and decompressing various formats. - [Features](#features) - [Usage](#usage) - [Installation](#installation) - [Supported Formats](#supported-formats) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Contributing](#contributing) # Features 1. Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## Compressing Pass input files to the `compress` subcommand, add the **output file** at the end. ```sh # Compress two files into `archive.zip` ouch compress one.txt two.txt archive.zip # Compress file.txt using .lz4 and .zst ouch compress file.txt file.txt.lz4.zst ``` `ouch` detects the extensions of the **output file** to decide what formats to use. ## Listing ```sh ouch list archive.zip # Example with tree formatting ouch list source-code.zip --tree ``` Output: ``` └── src ├── archive │ ├── mod.rs │ ├── tar.rs │ └── zip.rs ├── utils │ ├── colors.rs │ ├── formatting.rs │ ├── mod.rs │ └── fs.rs ├── commands │ ├── list.rs │ ├── compress.rs │ ├── decompress.rs │ └── mod.rs ├── accessible.rs ├── error.rs ├── cli.rs └── main.rs ``` # Supported formats | Format | `.tar` | `.zip` | `.7z` | `.gz` | `.sz` | `.zst` | `.xz` | `.lzma` | `.lz` | `.bz`, `.bz2` | `.bz3` | `.lz4` | `.rar` | `.br` | |:---------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Supported | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓¹ | ✓² | ✓² | ✓² | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓³ | ✓ | ✓: Supports compression and decompression. ✓¹: Due to limitations of the compression format itself, (de)compression can't be done with streaming. ✓²: Supported, and compression runs in parallel. ✓³: Due to RAR's restrictive license, only decompression and listing can be supported. If you wish to exclude non-free code from your build, you can disable RAR support by building without the `unrar` feature. Aliases for these formats are also supported: - `tar`: `tgz`, `tbz`, `tbz2`, `tlz4`, `txz`, `tlzma`, `tsz`, `tzst`, `tlz`, `cbt` - `zip`: `cbz`, `epub` - `7z`: `cb7` - `rar`: `cbr` Formats can be chained: - `.tar.gz` - `.tar.gz.xz.zst.gz.lz4.sz` If the filename has no extensions, `ouch` will try to infer the format by the [file signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_signatures) and ask the user for confirmation. # Installation Refer to the packages list on the right. The most commonly used installation methods: ## On Arch Linux ```bash pacman -S ouch ``` ## On MacOS via Homebrew ```bash brew install ouch ``` ## On Windows via Scoop ```cmd scoop install ouch ``` ## From crates.io ```bash cargo install ouch ``` (If you're on Ubuntu, you might need to install `clang` to build it from crates.io.) ## Download the latest release bundle Check the [releases page](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/releases). Release binaries are signed with [Sigstore](https://sigstore.dev) via GitHub's artifact attestations. Verify a downloaded binary with the GitHub CLI: ``` gh attestation verify ouch-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo ouch-org/ouch ``` ### Reproducing a release build Release builds are reproducible. Given the source at a tagged commit, anyone can rebuild the same binary and check that it matches what we shipped. Steps: ``` git clone https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch cd ouch git checkout export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --pretty=%ct) export RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$(pwd)=." cargo build --locked --release --target ``` The toolchain version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and rustup will install it automatically. Cross-compiled targets (anything using `cross-rs/cross`) inherit the cross Docker image's toolchain, which is not pinned by digest yet, so those targets are bit-for-bit reproducible only against the same `cross` image release. ## Compiling from source code Check the [wiki guide on compiling](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Compiling-and-installing-from-source-code). # Benchmarks Benchmark results are available [here](benchmarks/results.md). Performance of compressing and decompressing [Rust](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) source code is measured and compared with [Hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine). The values presented are the average (wall clock) elapsed time. Note: `ouch` focuses heavily on usage ergonomics and nice error messages, but we plan on doing some optimization in the future. Versions used: - `ouch` _0.4.0_ - [`tar`] _1.34_ - [`unzip`][infozip] _6.00_ - [`zip`][infozip] _3.0_ # Contributing Contributions of all sizes are welcome and appreciated! - Open an [issue](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/issues). - Package it for your favorite distribution or package manager. - Share it with a friend! - Open a pull request. If you're creating a Pull Request, check [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md). Added listing.py with stdlib ZIP/TAR archive entry extraction and flat/tree rendering via list_archive(path, tree=False), returning lines including `Archive: "..."`. Ready for CLI integration; currently preserves archive order and supports nested paths. I’ll continue probing tree quirks.

     1  import os
     2  import tarfile
     3  import zipfile

     5  
     6  def _tree(names):
     7      root = {}
     8      for raw in names:
     9          parts = [p for p in raw.split('/') if p]
    10          if not parts:
    11              continue
    12          node = root
    13          for part in parts:
    14              node = node.setdefault(part, {})
    15      out = []
    16      def walk(node, prefix=''):
    17          items = list(node.items())
    18          for i, (name, child) in enumerate(items):
    19              last = i == len(items)-1
    20              out.append(prefix + ('└── ' if last else '├── ') + name)
    21              walk(child, prefix + ('   ' if last else '│  '))
    22      walk(root)
    23      return out
    24  
    25  
    26  def list_archive(path, tree=False):
    27      """Return archive listing lines including the Archive header."""
    28      label = os.fspath(path)
    29      if zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
    30          with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
    31              names = [i.filename for i in z.infolist()]
    32      elif tarfile.is_tarfile(path):
    33          with tarfile.open(path, 'r:*') as t:
    34              names = [m.name.rstrip('/') + ('/' if m.isdir() else '') for m in t.getmembers()]
    35      else:
    36          raise ValueError('unsupported archive format')
    37      body = _tree(names) if tree else names
    38      return [f'Archive: "{label}"'] + body"}],"isError":false}

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/main.py
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import os, sys, pathlib, shutil, gzip, bz2, lzma
+from listing import list_archive
+from compression import compress
+from decompression import decompress_file, formats_for
+
+VERSION = 'ouch 0.8.0'
+EXTS = 'tar, zip, bz, bz2, bz3, gz, lz4, xz, lzma, lz, sz, zst, rar, 7z'
+ALIASES = 'tgz, tbz, tlz4, txz, tlzma, tsz, tzst, tlz, cbt, cbz, epub, cb7, cbr'
+ROOT_HELP = '''A command-line utility for easily compressing and decompressing files and directories.
+
+Usage: executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
+
+Commands:
+  compress    Compress one or more files into one output file [aliases: c]
+  decompress  Decompresses one or more files, optionally into another folder [aliases: d]
+  list        List contents of an archive [aliases: l, ls]
+  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)
+
+Options:
+  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
+  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
+  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
+  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
+  -q, --quiet                Silence output
+  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
+  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
+  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
+  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
+  -h, --help                 Print help (see more with '--help')
+  -V, --version              Print version
+'''
+COMMAND_HELP = {
+'compress': '''Compress one or more files into one output file
+
+Usage: executable compress [OPTIONS] <FILES>... <OUTPUT>
+
+Arguments:
+  <FILES>...  Files to be compressed
+  <OUTPUT>    The resulting file. Its extensions can be used to specify the compression formats
+
+Options:
+  -l, --level <LEVEL>        Compression level, applied to all formats
+  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
+      --fast                 Fastest compression level possible, conflicts with --level and --slow
+  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
+  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
+      --slow                 Slowest (and best) compression level possible, conflicts with --level and --fast
+  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
+  -S, --follow-symlinks      Read from target files instead of from symlinks (relevant for `tar` and `zip`)
+  -q, --quiet                Silence output
+  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
+  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
+  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
+  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
+  -h, --help                 Print help
+''',
+'decompress': '''Decompresses one or more files, optionally into another folder
+
+Usage: executable decompress [OPTIONS] <FILES>...
+
+Arguments:
+  <FILES>...  Files to be decompressed, or "-" for stdin
+
+Options:
+  -d, --dir <OUTPUT_DIR>     Decompress inside OUTPUT_DIR instead of the basename-derived subdirectory
+  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
+      --here                 Extract directly into the current directory, like `tar -xf` and `unzip` do
+  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
+  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
+  -r, --remove               Remove the source file after successful decompression
+  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
+  -q, --quiet                Silence output
+  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
+  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
+  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
+  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
+  -h, --help                 Print help
+''',
+'list': '''List contents of an archive
+
+Usage: executable list [OPTIONS] <ARCHIVES>...
+
+Arguments:
+  <ARCHIVES>...  Archives whose contents should be listed
+
+Options:
+  -t, --tree                 Show archive contents as a tree
+  -y, --yes                  Skip [Y/n] questions, default to yes
+  -n, --no                   Skip [Y/n] questions, default to no
+  -A, --accessible           Activate accessibility mode, reducing visual noise [env: ACCESSIBLE=]
+  -H, --hidden               Ignore hidden files
+  -q, --quiet                Silence output
+  -g, --gitignore            Ignore files matched by git's ignore files
+  -f, --format <FORMAT>      Specify the format of the archive
+  -p, --password <PASSWORD>  Decompress or list with password
+  -c, --threads <THREADS>    Concurrent working threads
+  -h, --help                 Print help
+'''}
+
+def die(msg, code=1):
+    print(msg, file=sys.stderr); raise SystemExit(code)
+
+def parse(argv, command):
+    opts={'yes':False,'no':False,'quiet':False,'format':None,'tree':False,'here':False,'dir':None,'remove':False,'level':None,'fast':False,'slow':False,'follow':False}
+    pos=[]; i=0
+    takes={'-f':'format','--format':'format','-p':'password','--password':'password','-c':'threads','--threads':'threads','-l':'level','--level':'level','-d':'dir','--dir':'dir'}
+    flags={'-y':'yes','--yes':'yes','-n':'no','--no':'no','-q':'quiet','--quiet':'quiet','-t':'tree','--tree':'tree','--here':'here','-r':'remove','--remove':'remove','--fast':'fast','--slow':'slow','-S':'follow','--follow-symlinks':'follow'}
+    while i<len(argv):
+        a=argv[i]
+        if a in ('-h','--help'): print(COMMAND_HELP[command],end=''); raise SystemExit(0)
+        if a in ('-A','--accessible','-H','--hidden','-g','--gitignore'): i+=1; continue
+        if a in flags: opts[flags[a]]=True
+        elif a.startswith('--') and '=' in a and a.split('=',1)[0] in takes:
+            k,v=a.split('=',1); opts[takes[k]]=v
+        elif a in takes:
+            i+=1
+            if i>=len(argv): die(f"error: a value is required for '{a}'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
+            opts[takes[a]]=argv[i]
+        elif a.startswith('-') and a!='-': die(f"error: unexpected argument '{a}' found\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
+        else: pos.append(a)
+        i+=1
+    if opts['fast'] and opts['slow']: die("error: the argument '--fast' cannot be used with '--slow'\n\nUsage: executable compress --fast <FILES>... <OUTPUT>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
+    if opts['fast'] and opts['level'] is not None or opts['slow'] and opts['level'] is not None: die("error: the argument '--level <LEVEL>' cannot be used with '--fast'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
+    if opts['here'] and opts['dir']: die("error: the argument '--here' cannot be used with '--dir <OUTPUT_DIR>'\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
+    if opts['level'] is not None:
+        try: opts['level']=int(opts['level'])
+        except: die(f"error: invalid value '{opts['level']}' for '--level <LEVEL>': invalid digit found in string\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
+    return opts,pos
+
+def missing(path):
+    die(f"[ERROR] failed to canonicalize path `{path}`: No such file or directory (os error 2)\n - File not found")
+
+def ext_formats(path, override=None):
+    if override: return [x.lower() for x in override.split('.') if x]
+    parts=pathlib.Path(path).name.split('.')
+    return [x.lower() for x in parts[1:] if x]
+
+def main(argv):
+    if not argv or argv[0] in ('-h','--help'): print(ROOT_HELP,end=''); return 0
+    if argv[0] in ('-V','--version'): print(VERSION); return 0
+    if argv[0]=='help':
+        cmd=argv[1] if len(argv)>1 else None
+        if cmd in ('c',): cmd='compress'
+        if cmd in ('d',): cmd='decompress'
+        if cmd in ('l','ls'): cmd='list'
+        print(COMMAND_HELP.get(cmd,ROOT_HELP),end=''); return 0
+    cmd=argv.pop(0); cmd={'c':'compress','d':'decompress','l':'list','ls':'list'}.get(cmd,cmd)
+    if cmd not in COMMAND_HELP: die(f"error: unrecognized subcommand '{cmd}'\n\nUsage: executable [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
+    opts,pos=parse(argv,cmd)
+    required={'compress':2,'decompress':1,'list':1}[cmd]
+    if len(pos)<required:
+        args={'compress':'  <FILES>...\n  <OUTPUT>','decompress':'  <FILES>...','list':'  <ARCHIVES>...'}[cmd]
+        if cmd=='compress' and len(pos)==1: args='  <FILES>...'
+        die(f"error: the following required arguments were not provided:\n{args}\n\nUsage: executable {cmd} {'<FILES>... <OUTPUT>' if cmd=='compress' else '<FILES>...' if cmd=='decompress' else '<ARCHIVES>...'}\n\nFor more information, try '--help'.",2)
+    if cmd=='compress':
+        inputs=pos[:-1]; output=pos[-1]
+        for p in inputs:
+            if not os.path.exists(p): missing(p)
+        fmts=ext_formats(output,opts['format'])
+        if not fmts:
+            die(f'[ERROR] Cannot compress to "{output}"\n - You must supply the compression format\n\nhint: Try adding supported extensions (see --help):\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output}.tar.gz\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output}.zip\nhint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can overwrite this option by using the \'--format\' flag:\nhint:   ouch compress <FILES>... {output} --format tar.gz')
+        try: compress(inputs,output,fmts,opts['level'],opts['follow'])
+        except Exception as e: die(f'[ERROR] {e}')
+        if not opts['quiet']:
+            print(f'[INFO] Compressing "{inputs[0]}"')
+            try: print(f'[INFO] Output file size: {os.path.getsize(output):.2f}   B')
+            except: pass
+            print(f'[INFO] Successfully compressed to "{output}"')
+        return 0
+    if cmd=='list':
+        for path in pos:
+            if not os.path.exists(path): missing(path)
+            try:
+                lines=list_archive(path,opts['tree'])
+                if opts['quiet']: lines=lines[1:]
+                for line in lines: print(line)
+            except Exception:
+                die(f'[ERROR] Cannot list archive contents\n - Only archives can have their contents listed\n - Files are not archives: "{path}"')
+        return 0
+    for path in pos:
+        if path!='-' and not os.path.exists(path): missing(path)
+        fmts=ext_formats(path,opts['format'])
+        if not fmts:
+            die(f'[ERROR] Cannot decompress files\n - Files with missing extensions: "{path}"\n - Decompression formats are detected automatically from file extension and signature\n\nhint: Supported extensions are: {EXTS}\nhint: Supported aliases are: {ALIASES}\nhint: \nhint: Alternatively, you can pass an extension to the \'--format\' flag:\nhint:   ouch decompress {path} --format tar.gz')
+        try:
+            dest,count=decompress_file(path,opts['dir'],opts['here'],opts['format'])
+            if opts['remove'] and path!='-': os.remove(path)
+            if not opts['quiet']:
+                if path=='-': print('[INFO] STDIN decompressed to "ouch-output"')
+                else: print(f'[INFO] Decompressed "{path}" to "{dest}"')
+                print(f'[INFO] Decompressed {count} files')
+        except Exception as e: die(f'[ERROR] Cannot decompress files\n - {e}')
+    return 0
+
+if __name__=='__main__':
+    try: raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
+    except BrokenPipeError: raise SystemExit(1)
*** End Patch";

if os.fspath(path) == "-":
        return "ouch-output"
    name = os.path.basename(os.fspath(path))
    values = formats if formats is not None else formats_for(path)
    parts = name.split(".")
    raw_suffix = parts[-1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""
    strip_count = 1 if raw_suffix in ALIASES else len(values)
    if strip_count and len(parts) > strip_count:
        name = ".".join(parts[:-strip_count])
    if not name:
        name = "ouch-output"
    return name


def _safe_target(root, name):
    # Reject absolute paths and traversal, including Windows separators.
    name = name.replace("\\", "/")
    p = pathlib.PurePosixPath(name)
    if p.is_absolute() or ".." in p.parts:
        return None
    target = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(root, *p.parts))
    if os.path.commonpath((os.path.abspath(root), target)) != os.path.abspath(root):
        return None
    return target

content.text:
## Task and constraints

Reimplement `/opt/reference/executable` (`ouch 0.8.0`) in Python 3.10 using only the standard library. The reference is for behavioral observation only. Do not run `compile.sh`; verify with `python3 main.py ...`. The shared `team/main` branch is the graded submission, so fetch, merge, and push changes there.

## Progress

CLI integration is implemented in `main.py`, connected to `compression.py`, `decompression.py`, and `listing.py`. It supports commands and aliases, help/version, common options, format inference and errors, ZIP/TAR/stream operations, signature fallback, conflict handling, and output logs. Teammates have contributed and refined the helper modules.

The latest local branch was synced from `team/main` at commit `2a976b5`; it was clean at that point. Work has been pushed throughout the session. Always fetch before the next push because teammates are updating the shared branch frequently.

Help output was compared with the reference and matched for `-h`, `--help`, `help`, command help, and `--version`. Syntax checks and smoke comparisons for ZIP/TAR, stream-wrapped ZIP, signature-detected extensionless TAR, thread validation, and error messages passed.

## Critical next step

The latest reference probe found output stream differences that still need fixing:

- `compress` status messages go to **stderr**. Probe: reference compression placed all `[INFO]` lines in stderr and nothing in stdout.
- `decompress` status messages go to **stderr**. Probe: directory creation, extracted member, success, and unpack count all appeared in stderr.
- `list` archive header and member names go to **stdout**.
- Error messages are already written to stderr.

The current implementation likely prints compression/decompression status messages to stdout. Update those messages to stderr while keeping list output on stdout. Then compare stdout and stderr separately against the reference for compress, decompress, and list, run `python3 -m py_compile` on the modules, and push the fix to `team/main`.

## Reference observations

- `compress a.txt out.foo` emits missing-format hints; absolute paths under cwd are displayed relative to cwd.
- `decompress --here` conflicts with `--dir`; `--fast` conflicts with `--slow`; `--yes` conflicts with `--no`.
- `--threads abc` is invalid; zero is accepted. `--level -1` as a separate token is an unexpected argument.
- `--quiet list archive.zip` suppresses the archive header but retains members.
- Empty TAR listing emits a format sniff notice.
- Stream-wrapped ZIP operations warn that ZIP chaining requires in-memory processing.
- Uppercase/unrecognized extensions can fall back to signature detection.
- `--hidden` does not filter hidden members during decompression; the reference extracted `.secret` in the probe.
- `/workspace/test_assets/test_resources/` contains the reference help snapshots used by the implementation.

## Current communication

Group channel posts record the feature map, findings, commits, and integration. Continue checking the group feed and latest `team/main` before editing to avoid duplicate work.
I’ll inspect the latest shared branch and read the relevant group updates, then fix the stdout/stderr mismatch in the integrated CLI and push it.

# Ouch! `ouch` stands for **Obvious Unified Compression Helper**. It's a CLI tool for compressing and decompressing various formats. - [Features](#features) - [Usage](#usage) - [Installation](#installation) - [Supported Formats](#supported-formats) - [Benchmarks](#benchmarks) - [Contributing](#contributing) # Features 1. Easy to use. 2. Fast. 3. Great error message feedback. 4. No runtime dependencies. 5. Accessibility mode ([see more](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Accessibility)). 6. Shell completions and man pages. # Usage `ouch` has three main subcommands: - `ouch decompress` (alias `d`) - `ouch compress` (alias `c`) - `ouch list` (alias `l` or `ls`) To see `help` for a specific command: ```sh ouch help ouch --help # equivalent ``` ## Decompressing Use the `decompress` subcommand, `ouch` will detect the extensions automatically. ```sh ouch decompress a.zip # Decompress multiple files ouch decompress a.zip b.tar.gz c.tar ``` The `-d/--dir` flag can be used to redirect decompression results to another directory. ```sh # Decompress 'summer_vacation.zip' inside of new folder 'pictures' ouch decompress summer_vacation.zip --dir pictures ``` ## Compressing Pass input files to the `compress` subcommand, add the **output file** at the end. ```sh # Compress two files into `archive.zip` ouch compress one.txt two.txt archive.zip # Compress file.txt using .lz4 and .zst ouch compress file.txt file.txt.lz4.zst ``` `ouch` detects the extensions of the **output file** to decide what formats to use. ## Listing ```sh ouch list archive.zip # Example with tree formatting ouch list source-code.zip --tree ``` Output: ``` └── src ├── archive │ ├── mod.rs │ ├── tar.rs │ └── zip.rs ├── utils │ ├── colors.rs │ ├── formatting.rs │ ├── mod.rs │ └── fs.rs ├── commands │ ├── list.rs │ ├── compress.rs │ ├── decompress.rs │ └── mod.rs ├── accessible.rs ├── error.rs ├── cli.rs └── main.rs ``` # Supported formats | Format | `.tar` | `.zip` | `.7z` | `.gz` | `.sz` | `.zst` | `.xz` | `.lzma` | `.lz` | `.bz`, `.bz2` | `.bz3` | `.lz4` | `.rar` | `.br` | |:---------:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Supported | ✓ | ✓¹ | ✓¹ | ✓² | ✓² | ✓² | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓³ | ✓ | ✓: Supports compression and decompression. ✓¹: Due to limitations of the compression format itself, (de)compression can't be done with streaming. ✓²: Supported, and compression runs in parallel. ✓³: Due to RAR's restrictive license, only decompression and listing can be supported. If you wish to exclude non-free code from your build, you can disable RAR support by building without the `unrar` feature. Aliases for these formats are also supported: - `tar`: `tgz`, `tbz`, `tbz2`, `tlz4`, `txz`, `tlzma`, `tsz`, `tzst`, `tlz`, `cbt` - `zip`: `cbz`, `epub` - `7z`: `cb7` - `rar`: `cbr` Formats can be chained: - `.tar.gz` - `.tar.gz.xz.zst.gz.lz4.sz` If the filename has no extensions, `ouch` will try to infer the format by the [file signature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_signatures) and ask the user for confirmation. # Installation Refer to the packages list on the right. The most commonly used installation methods: ## On Arch Linux ```bash pacman -S ouch ``` ## On MacOS via Homebrew ```bash brew install ouch ``` ## On Windows via Scoop ```cmd scoop install ouch ``` ## From crates.io ```bash cargo install ouch ``` (If you're on Ubuntu, you might need to install `clang` to build it from crates.io.) ## Download the latest release bundle Check the [releases page](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/releases). Release binaries are signed with [Sigstore](https://sigstore.dev) via GitHub's artifact attestations. Verify a downloaded binary with the GitHub CLI: ``` gh attestation verify ouch-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --repo ouch-org/ouch ``` ### Reproducing a release build Release builds are reproducible. Given the source at a tagged commit, anyone can rebuild the same binary and check that it matches what we shipped. Steps: ``` git clone https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch cd ouch git checkout export SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=$(git log -1 --pretty=%ct) export RUSTFLAGS="--remap-path-prefix=$(pwd)=." cargo build --locked --release --target ``` The toolchain version is pinned in `rust-toolchain.toml` and rustup will install it automatically. Cross-compiled targets (anything using `cross-rs/cross`) inherit the cross Docker image's toolchain, which is not pinned by digest yet, so those targets are bit-for-bit reproducible only against the same `cross` image release. ## Compiling from source code Check the [wiki guide on compiling](https://github.com/ouch-org/ouch/wiki/Compiling-and-installing-from-source-code). # Benchmarks Benchmark results are available [here](benchmarks/results.md). Performance of compressing and decompressing [Rust](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust) source code is measured and compared with [Hyperfine](https://github.com/sharkdp/hyperfine). The values presented are the average (wall clock) elapsed time. Note: `ouch` focuses heavily on usage ergonomics and nice error messages, but we plan on doing some optimization in the future. Versions used: - `ouch` _0.4.0_ "}

"""ZIP/TAR output helpers for ouch-compatible compression."""
import bz2
import gzip
import fnmatch
import lzma
import os
import stat
import struct
import zlib
import tarfile
import zipfile


def _members(paths, follow_symlinks=False, ignore_hidden=False, use_gitignore=False):
    """Yield archive members in the host filesystem's depth-first order."""
    def read_patterns(directory, base):
        rules=[]
        if not use_gitignore: return rules
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(directory,'.gitignore'),encoding='utf-8',errors='replace') as f:
                for raw in f:
                    pat=raw.strip()
                    if not pat or pat.startswith('#'): continue
                    neg=pat.startswith('!')
                    if neg: pat=pat[1:]
                    prefix=os.path.relpath(directory,base).replace(os.sep,'/')
                    if prefix=='.': prefix=''
                    rules.append((prefix,pat,neg))
        except OSError: pass
        return rules

    def ignored(rel, is_dir, rules):
        rel=rel.replace(os.sep,'/')
        skip=False
        for prefix,pat,neg in rules:
            if pat.startswith('\\#') or pat.startswith('\\!'): pat=pat[1:]
            target=rel[len(prefix)+1:] if prefix and rel.startswith(prefix+'/') else ('' if rel==prefix else rel)
            if prefix and not (rel==prefix or rel.startswith(prefix+'/')): continue
            directory_only=pat.endswith('/')
            pat=pat.strip('/')
            anchored='/' in pat
            parts=target.split('/')
            matched=fnmatch.fnmatchcase(target,pat) if anchored else any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase(part,pat) for part in parts)
            if directory_only and not is_dir and not matched:
                matched=any(fnmatch.fnmatchcase('/'.join(parts[:i]),pat) for i in range(1,len(parts)))
            if matched: skip=not neg
        return skip

    def descend(directory, base, rules):
        rules=rules+read_patterns(directory,base)
        try:
            entries = list(os.scandir(directory))
        except OSError:
            return
        for entry in entries:
            if ignore_hidden and entry.name.startswith('.'):
                continue
            full = entry.path
            rel=os.path.relpath(full,base)
            is_dir=entry.is_dir(follow_symlinks=follow_symlinks)
            if use_gitignore and ignored(rel,is_dir,rules): continue
            yield full, rel
            if is_dir:
                yield from descend(full, base, rules)

    for src in paths:
        src = os.fspath(src)
        name = os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(src)) or src
        if os.path.islink(src) and not follow_symlinks:
            yield src, name
            if os.path.isdir(src):
                base = os.path.dirname(os.path.normpath(src)) or "."
                yield from descend(src, base, read_patterns(base, base))
        elif os.path.isdir(src):
            yield src, name
            base = os.path.dirname(os.path.normpath(src)) or "."
            yield from descend(src, base, read_patterns(base, base))
        else:
            yield src, name


def compress(inputs, output, formats=None, level=None, follow_symlinks=False, ignore_hidden=False, use_gitignore=False):
    """Create ZIP/TAR and optional stream layers. Returns output path.

    ``formats`` are ordered inner-to-outer, e.g. ["tar", "gz"].
    """
    formats = [str(x).lower().lstrip(".") for x in (formats or [])]
    aliases = {"tgz": ["tar", "gz"], "tbz": ["tar", "bz2"],
               "tbz2": ["tar", "bz2"], "txz": ["tar", "xz"],
               "tlzma": ["tar", "lzma"], "tzst": ["tar", "zst"],
               "tlz": ["tar", "lz"], "tlz4": ["tar", "lz4"],
               "tsz": ["tar", "sz"], "cbt": ["tar"], "cbz": ["zip"], "epub": ["zip"],
               "cb7": ["7z"]}
    if len(formats) == 1 and formats[0] in aliases:
        formats = aliases[formats[0]]
    if not formats:
        raise ValueError("compression format required")
    if formats[0] not in ("zip", "tar"):
        stream_formats = {"gz", "bz", "bz2", "xz", "lzma"}
        if all(f in stream_formats for f in formats) and len(inputs) == 1:
            with open(os.fspath(inputs[0]), "rb") as inp:
                data = inp.read()
            gzip_level = 1 if level is None else max(1, min(9, int(level)))
            level = 9 if level is None else max(0, min(9, int(level)))
            for fmt in formats:
                if fmt == "gz":
                    data = gzip.compress(data, compresslevel=gzip_level, mtime=0)
                elif fmt in ("bz", "bz2"):
                    data = bz2.compress(data, compresslevel=max(1, level))
                else:
                    data = lzma.compress(data, preset=level)
            with open(output, "wb") as raw:
                raw.write(data)
            return output
        raise ValueError("unsupported compression format")
    if formats[0] == "zip":
        import io
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        zip_level = 1 if level is None else max(0, min(9, int(level)))
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=zip_level) as zf:
            for src, arc in _members(inputs, follow_symlinks, ignore_hidden, use_gitignore):
                if os.path.islink(src) and not follow_symlinks:
                    payload = os.readlink(src).encode()
                    info = zipfile.ZipInfo(arc)
                    info.create_system = 3
                    info.external_attr = (stat.S_IFLNK | 0o777) << 16
                elif os.path.isdir(src):
                    payload = b""
                    info = zipfile.ZipInfo(arc.rstrip("/") + "/")
                    info.create_system = 3
                    info.external_attr = (stat.S_IFDIR | 0o755) << 16
                    info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_STORED
                else:
                    with open(src, "rb") as member:
                        payload = member.read()
                    info = zipfile.ZipInfo.from_file(src, arc)
                if not os.path.isdir(src):
                    info.compress_type = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED
                compressed_size = 0 if info.compress_type == zipfile.ZIP_STORED else _deflated_size(payload, zip_level)
                info.extra = struct.pack("<HHQQ", 1, 16, len(payload), compressed_size)
                zf.writestr(info, payload, compress_type=info.compress_type, compresslevel=zip_level)
        data = buf.getvalue()
        for fmt in formats[1:]:
            data = _encode(data, fmt, level)
        with open(output, "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
    else:
        mode = "w"
        tar_name = output
        outer = formats[1:]
        # Build tar in memory before applying stream compression layers.
        import io
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=buf, mode="w", format=tarfile.GNU_FORMAT, dereference=follow_symlinks) as tf:
            for src, arc in _members(inputs, follow_symlinks, ignore_hidden, use_gitignore):
                tf.add(src, arcname=arc, recursive=False)
        data = buf.getvalue()
        # Keep the two mandatory end-of-archive blocks, but discard Python's
        # extra record padding after them.
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(data), mode="r:") as check:
            members = check.getmembers()
        end = max((m.offset_data + ((m.size + 511) // 512) * 512 for m in members), default=0)
        data = bytearray(data[:end + 1024])
        for member in members:
            offset = member.offset
            header = bytearray(data[offset:offset + 512])
            kind = stat.S_IFDIR if member.isdir() else stat.S_IFLNK if member.issym() else stat.S_IFREG
            header[100:108] = f"{kind | (member.mode & 0o7777):07o}".encode() + b"\0"
            header[265:329] = b"\0" * 64
            header[329:337] = b"0000000\0"
            header[337:345] = b"0000000\0"
            header[148:156] = b" " * 8
            header[148:156] = f"{sum(header):07o}".encode() + b"\0"
            data[offset:offset + 512] = header
        data = bytes(data)
        for fmt in outer:
            data = _encode(data, fmt, level)
        with open(tar_name, "wb") as f:
            f.write(data)
    return output


def _copy(source, target):
    while True:
        chunk = source.read(1024 * 1024)
        if not chunk:
            break
        target.write(chunk)


def _encode(data, fmt, level):
    if fmt == "gz":
        # Stream compressor default is tuned separately from standalone gzip;
        # this keeps tar/ZIP stream layers close to Ouch's encoding output.
        gzip_level = 3 if level is None else max(1, min(9, int(level)))
        return gzip.compress(data, compresslevel=gzip_level, mtime=0)
    level = 9 if level is None else max(0, min(9, int(level)))
    if fmt in ("bz", "bz2"):
        return bz2.compress(data, compresslevel=max(1, level))
    if fmt in ("xz", "lzma"):
        return lzma.compress(data, preset=level)
    raise ValueError("unsupported compression format")


def _deflated_size(data, level):
    compressor = zlib.compressobj(1 if level is None else max(0, min(9, int(level))), zlib.DEFLATED, -15)
    return len(compressor.compress(data) + compressor.flush())
